description: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE of kye:registry:separation-of-duties. One worked row, not the full set — the live registry is the source of truth and is not duplicated here (§0). Present so the schema has a validated instance a reader and the ajv corpus can both use.

duty_pairs.buys: A page writer's own --check compares its fresh output to disk, which cannot see that a DIFFERENT writer's region was destroyed on the way — the producer has no reason to know a region it does not own exists. The umbrella verifier runs every generator and diffs the whole tree, so a page that lost bytes to another writer surfaces even though each writer individually reports clean. This is the pair that failed in the observable way: 628 pages were stripped and every individual generator was green.

anti_patterns.name: self-certifying generator
anti_patterns.definition: A generator whose --check is the only thing verifying its output. Cheap and useful as a first signal; fatal as the sole one, because it can only compare against the shape it just produced.

honest_scope: This binds KYE's OWN duty pairs. It does not claim organisational separation of duties for a customer deployment — that is a §36 GovernedUI approval-mode question (two_person, two_person_with_legal), governed elsewhere and not restated here (§0). Conflating the two would let an engineering-hygiene gate read as a control attestation, which is the §70 dishonesty line.

enforcement.contract: Every duty pair names a producer and a verifier that is a DIFFERENT actor, and that verifier must resolve on disk AND be wired into npm test. A verifier that is the producer, does not exist, or is not runnable is self-certification with a second name on it.
